rv.q: Whatever problems there may be with this production, which reaches for the sky with short if well-shaped arms, Mrs. Johnson qualifies as a blessing for those in search of signs of intelligent life in the American musical.
Despite the show’s admirable intelligence, however, the elements fail to jell.
I call it rapturous and thoroughly ravishing.

He may want that lineage downplayed when he’s reviewed, but he apparently doesn’t get away from it when putting a melody together. This is a good thing, of course: Rodgers wrote some of the most passionate music ever to grace a stage, the sort of music that composers can’t write today or, more’s the pity, are reluctant to write.
The number soars easily, but has difficulty landing.

cn.t: Critics praise Guettel's ambitious, lush score and Victoria Clark's poignant performance, though most find the show itself unfulfilled and problematic despite its exquisite production values.

vs.sum: The Vivian Beaumont Theater offers exceptional sightlines and sound quality due to its unique thrust stage design, ensuring a great view and auditory experience from nearly every seat. While the ambiance is enhanced by its location within the Lincoln Center, the comfort level is average with some reports of tight seating, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue.

acc.note: Orchestra accessible via elevator. Induction hearing loop for t-coil. Loge NOT accessible (stairs only).
